items.streetShift: Brings intense focus to the subject: 'ร้อนมากเนี่ย' (It is SO hot right now!), 'คนนี้เนี่ย' (THIS person right here).
items.situationPrompt: Someone is complaining about Bangkok traffic and says 'Rot dtit maak nîa!'. What feeling does 'เนี่ย' add?
items.situationCorrect: Emphasis & personal exasperation about the immediate situation
situationDistractors: It turns the sentence into a polite apology
It makes the sentence formal for news broadcast
It indicates future tense

items.streetShift: The warmest, most bonding conversational ending. 'Aroi nor!' (So delicious, right?!). Prompts the listener to nod in mutual agreement.
items.situationPrompt: You take a bite of fresh mango sticky rice and turn to your partner to share the mutual joy: 'Aroi nór!'. What does 'เนาะ' express?
items.situationCorrect: 'Right?! Don't you agree?' — bonding consensus
situationDistractors: A stern warning not to eat it
A polite refusal
A question asking what time it is

items.streetShift: Heard in almost every casual Thai sentence: 'อะไรอ่ะ' (What's that?), 'เค้าอ่ะ' (As for him...). Relaxes any sentence from sounding stiff.
items.situationPrompt: Why do Thai native speakers attach 'อะ' (à) to the ends of questions like 'ทำไมอ่ะ' or statements like 'ก็ดีอ่ะ'?
items.situationCorrect: It softens the sentence and makes it naturally casual among friends
situationDistractors: It is a strict grammar requirement for negative verbs
It marks past tense actions
It is only used when angry

items.streetShift: Super-versatile particle! 'ไปเลย' (go right now!), 'ไม่ชอบเลย' (don't like it at all!), 'ดีเลย' (that's awesome!).
items.situationPrompt: Your friend suggests going to the night market and you enthusiastically agree: 'Pai loei!'. What does 'เลย' mean here?
items.situationCorrect: 'Right now! / Let's go immediately!'
situationDistractors: Maybe tomorrow
I don't have money
Turn left

items.spoken: rǒe / rɔ̌ɔ (หรอ/เหรอออ)
items.streetShift: Spoken with rising tone. When elongated to 'rǒeeeee?' it expresses humorous skepticism or playful shock.
items.situationPrompt: A friend tells you an incredible piece of gossip. You react with surprise: 'Jing rǒe?!' (จริงเหรอ). What are you asking?
items.situationCorrect: 'Really?! Is that true?!'
situationDistractors: Where did you hear that?
Who told you?
I already knew that

items.streetShift: 'กินสิ' (Eat up!), 'มาสิ' (Come on in!). Softens commands while encouraging action.
items.situationPrompt: You are hesitating to try a spicy street snack. A friend smiles and says 'Kin sì!'. What are they saying?
items.situationCorrect: 'Go ahead, eat it! Try it!'
situationDistractors: Don't touch that food
Pay for that first
It is not cooked yet

items.streetShift: Turns commands into polite, sweet requests: 'รอแป๊บนะ' (Wait a sec, okay?), 'ไปก่อนนะ' (I'm heading out, ok?).
items.situationPrompt: Why is 'นะ' (ná) considered the friendliest particle in the Thai language?
items.situationCorrect: It adds warmth, sweetness, and gentle agreement to statements
situationDistractors: It is strictly used by monks
It marks government orders
It indicates an angry tone

items.streetShift: 'แล้วเธอล่ะ' (And what about you?), 'แล้วไงล่ะ' (So what about it?). Bounces the topic back to the listener.
items.situationPrompt: You tell someone your food order, then turn to them and ask: 'Láew thoe lâ?'. What does 'ล่ะ' mean here?
items.situationCorrect: 'And what about you?'
situationDistractors: Where are you going?
How much is your meal?
Why aren't you eating?

items.streetShift: Textbooks teach ผม (phǒm) and ดิฉัน (dì-chǎn). But in casual speech with peers, Thais constantly refer to themselves as 'เรา' (rao).
items.situationPrompt: A Thai peer says 'เราอยากกินส้มตำ' (Rao yàak kin sôm-dtam). Who is 'เรา' referring to here?
items.situationCorrect: 'I / me' — casual friendly first-person pronoun
situationDistractors: The king or royalty
A stranger across the street
An old teacher

items.meaning: He / she / they (or cute 'I' among partners)
items.streetShift: The spoken version of เขา. Used for third persons ('เค้าบอกว่า...' - they said that...), and also used cutely as 'me' among couples.
items.situationPrompt: You hear someone say 'เค้าไม่ไป' (Kháo mâi bpai). What does 'เค้า' mean?
items.situationCorrect: He / She / They are not going
situationDistractors: We are going together
The car isn't moving
It's not delicious

items.streetShift: Heard constantly among close friends and couples as an endearing term for 'you' ('ตัวเองกินอะไรดี' - babe/you, what do you wanna eat?).
items.situationPrompt: A Thai couple is deciding on dinner and one asks 'ตัวเองอยากกินอะไร?'. What does 'ตัวเอง' mean in this context?
items.situationCorrect: 'You / Babe / Honey'
situationDistractors: The waiter
The chef
Yesterday's dinner

items.spoken: jing rǒe / jing dì (จริงดิ)
items.streetShift: The quintessential Thai conversation reactor. Alternates with 'จริงดิ?!' (jing dì) for peak youth slang.
items.situationPrompt: Someone tells you they saw a famous actor at 7-Eleven. What is the most natural reflex exclamation in Thai?
items.situationCorrect: จริงเหรอ?! / จริงดิ?! (jing rǒe / jing dì) — For real?!
situationDistractors: ขอบคุณครับ (khɔ̀ɔp-khun kháp) — Thank you
ไม่เป็นไร (mâi bpen rai) — Never mind
ตรงไป (drong bpai) — Go straight

items.meaning: 'No worries! / It is all good! / You are welcome!'
items.streetShift: Thailand's cultural mantra: cushions minor inconveniences, accepts apologies, and gracefully says 'You're welcome'.
items.situationPrompt: Someone accidentally bumps into you at a crowded BTS station and immediately apologizes. What is the classic Thai response?
items.situationCorrect: ไม่เป็นไรครับ/ค่ะ (mâi bpen rai) — No worries at all!
situationDistractors: เก็บตังค์ (gèp dtang) — Bill please
เท่าไหร่ (thâo-lài) — How much
จริงเหรอ (jing rǒe) — Really

items.streetShift: Casual enthusiastic acceptance of an invitation. 'ไปกินหมูกระทะกัน' (Let's go get Thai BBQ) -> 'เอาดิ!' (I'm so down!).
items.situationPrompt: Your friends propose going to an outdoor night market right now. You are 100% on board. What quick casual slang do you say?
items.situationCorrect: เอาดิ! (ao dì) — I'm down! Let's do it!
situationDistractors: ไม่เอา (mâi ao) — I don't want it
งงมาก (ngong mâak) — Confused
ไม่เป็นไร (mâi bpen rai) — No worries

items.streetShift: Everyday exclamation when directions are messy or a situation makes zero sense.
items.situationPrompt: A vendor explains a complicated system of queue tickets and you have no idea what's happening. What phrase expresses 'I am totally confused!'?
items.situationCorrect: งงมาก (ngong mâak) — So confused!
situationDistractors: โคตรดี (khôot dii) — Insanely good
เอาดิ (ao dì) — I'm down
สุดยอด (sùt yɔ̂ɔt) — Awesome

items.streetShift: โคตร (khôot) is ubiquitous slang replacing 'มาก' (very) for dramatic emphasis. Highly casual with friends.
items.situationPrompt: You try a legendary mango sticky rice and want to tell your buddy it's 'insanely good' using real street slang. What do you say?
items.situationCorrect: โคตรดี! (khôot dii) — Insanely good!
situationDistractors: งงมาก (ngong mâak) — Confused
ไม่หวาน (mâi wǎan) — Unsweetened
ตรงไป (drong bpai) — Go straight

items.streetShift: The #1 praise word in Thailand for great performances, delicious food, or amazing view points.
items.situationPrompt: A street cook performs a spectacular flaming wok show and serves you a masterpiece. What exclamation of praise do you give?
items.situationCorrect: สุดยอด! (sùt yɔ̂ɔt) — Awesome! Top tier!
situationDistractors: ไม่เอาถุง (mâi ao thǔng) — No bag
งงมาก (ngong mâak) — So confused
เก็บตังค์ (gèp dtang) — Check please

items.streetShift: Loanword from English 'chill' with Thai reduplication (ๆ). Means relaxing, taking it easy, or that a task is no stress.
items.situationPrompt: A friend asks if your schedule today is stressful. You reply 'Chil-chil!'. What does that communicate?
items.situationCorrect: Super relaxed, easy-going, no stress
situationDistractors: Extremely hectic and busy
Freezing cold weather
Need to visit the hospital

items.meaning: 'What should we do? / What is the move?'
items.streetShift: The go-to question when deciding where to eat, where to go out, or when plans suddenly change.
items.situationPrompt: Sudden tropical rain hits while you and your Thai friend are walking outdoors. Your friend looks at you and asks 'เอาไงดี?'. What are they asking?
items.situationCorrect: 'What should we do now? / What's the plan?'
situationDistractors: Can you lend me cash?
Where did you buy your umbrella?
Do you want to eat noodles?

curriculum.title: Street Food & Noodle Stalls
curriculum.subtitle: Order noodles, broth, custom toppings & takeout like a local

nodes.title: Noodle Kitchen Shorthand
nodes.description: Gradual buildup: lék (thin noodles) → yâak nám (broth separate) → mìi hâeng (dry egg noodles) → mâi chín mâi ngôok (no meatballs/sprouts) → full compound order

nodes.title: Spice & Topping Customization
nodes.description: Customizing ingredients: phèt nɔ́ɔi (mild heat) → mâi sài phrík (zero chilies) → mâi sài phàk-chii (no cilantro) → mâi sài phǒng-chuu-rót (no MSG)

nodes.title: Vendor Exchanges & Takeaway
nodes.description: Vendor questions & takeout: kin nîi rǒe sài hɔ̀ɔ (eat here or wrap to-go?) → sài hɔ̀ɔ (takeaway) → phí-sèet (extra portion)

curriculum.title: Cafes, 7-Eleven & Cashless Paying
curriculum.subtitle: Control sweetness, order ice, grab straws & scan PromptPay QR

nodes.title: Sweetness & Ice Customization
nodes.description: Cafe sweetness & ice: wǎan nɔ́ɔi (50% sweet) → mâi wǎan (0% sugar) → nám-khɛ̌ng bplào (cup of crushed ice) → wǎan bpòk-gà-dtì (normal)

nodes.title: Paying the Bill & Shorthand
nodes.description: Paying the bill: gèp dtang (check please) → thâo-lài (how much) → sà-gaen dâi mǎi (can I scan PromptPay QR?)

nodes.title: 7-Eleven Checkout Essentials
nodes.description: 7-Eleven checkout: mâi ao thǔng (no plastic bag) → mii lɔ̀ɔt mǎi (have a straw?) → wéep dâi mǎi (heat/microwave this up?)

curriculum.title: Taxis, Grab, Bolt & Navigation
curriculum.subtitle: Direct drivers smoothly, call polite titles & give rapid turns

nodes.title: Polite Addressing for Drivers & Peers
nodes.description: Polite titles: phîi kháp/khá (brother / driver / peer) → nɔ́ɔng kháp/khá (younger server / barista)

nodes.title: Turn-by-Turn Navigation
nodes.description: Turn-by-turn navigation: drong bpai (straight) → líaw sáai (turn left) → líaw kwǎa (turn right)

nodes.title: Pulling Over & Exact Stops
nodes.description: Pulling over & stops: jɔ̀ɔt drong níi (pull over right here) → khâang nâa (up ahead) → sɔɔi níi (this alley) → sòng thîi nîi (drop me here)

curriculum.title: Spoken Sound Shifts & Contractions
curriculum.subtitle: How Thais actually pronounce words vs formal written rules

nodes.title: Everyday ร → ล Sound Shifts
nodes.description: Everyday spoken shifts: à-lai (what? ร→ล shift) → kháp (dropped r-cluster) → à-lòi (delicious! ร→ล shift)

nodes.title: Rapid Street Contractions
nodes.description: Fast street contractions: bpào? (or not?) → ngíi (like this) → ngán (in that case)

nodes.title: Casual Conversational Question Words
nodes.description: Daily rhythm: bpáep-nɯng (one second!) → tham-mai (why?) → châi bpà (right? / isn't it?)

curriculum.title: Everyday Particles & Vibe Markers
curriculum.subtitle: The untranslatable feelings, social markers & tone shifters

nodes.title: Focus & Social Agreement Particles
nodes.description: Focus & consensus particles: nîa (right here! / emphasis) → nór (bonding agreement: right?!) → à (conversational softener)

nodes.title: Urgency, Imperatives & Reaction Tone
nodes.description: Imperatives & reactions: loei (right now! / totally!) → rǒe (really?!) → sì (go ahead! / do it!)

nodes.title: Sweet Softeners & Counter-Questions
nodes.description: Everyday warmth: ná (gentle reminder / softener) → lâ (what about...?)

curriculum.title: Casual Pronouns, Slang & Reactions
curriculum.subtitle: Natural friend talk, playful reactions & street lingo

nodes.title: Real-Life Casual Pronouns
nodes.description: Casual pronouns: rao (friendly I/me) → kháo (he/she/cute me) → dtua-eeng (you/babe)

nodes.title: Everyday Thai Reactions
nodes.description: Essential Thai reactions: jing rǒe (for real?!) → mâi bpen rai (no worries!) → ao dì (I'm down!)

nodes.title: Modern Bangkok Slang & Group Moves
nodes.description: Youth slang & moves: ngong mâak (baffled) → khôot dii (crazy good) → sùt yɔ̂ɔt (awesome) → chil-chil (relaxed) → ao ngai dii (what's the plan?)
